To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
electromagnetic exposure of cells during cytokinesis may help to explain TTFields’ anti-tumour effect.
the electromagnetic exposure of cells during telophase/cykinesis is the most likely cause for the anti-prolifterative effect of TTFs.
tumour-treating fields reduce proliferation by increasing the specific absorption rate at the furrow during mitosis.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of an electromagnetic model of the mitosis cell, the validation of this model by numerical electromagnetic simulations, and the validation of the model by experiments on cell cultures.
the development of a better understanding of the anti-prolifterative effect of TTFields on tumour cells and may help to improve TTFields application in future.
the development and validation of a lumped element model for the analysis of the electromagnetic exposure of cells during the mitotic phases.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
TTFields are a novel treatment modality for glioblastoma and other solid tumours.
TTFields are able to induce apoptosis by interfering with the chromosome separation process during mitosis.
the anti-prolificative effect of TTFields on tumours may be explained by the interference with the chromosome separation at the mitotic spindle during cytokinesis.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the anti-prolific effect of TTFields on cells is based on the electromagnetically increased power absorption in the cell membrane of dividing cells.
the electromagnetic field distribution in a mitotic cell depends on the cell cycle phase, which may lead to different effects on the cell’s behaviour.
the anti-prolific effect of TTFields is caused by an increase in the SAR in the mitotic cell at the mitotic cell furrow.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the mitotic furrows of cells are the main targets for electromagnetic exposure.

electromagnetic exposure of cells during cytokinesis can induce a local increase of specific absorption rate (as a measure of power absorption density) at the mitotic cell structure, the mitotic furrows, and that the anti-prolifterative effect is dependent on the frequency and commutation time of TTFields.
the electric fields are able to increase the SAR in the furrow region during mitosis and cytokinesis, which may help to induce cell apoptosis and thus to reduce tumour growth.
